subject: Post-call recap: procurement path, PO vs card, and approvals mapping (Acme Corp)
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Jones <sarah.jones@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 14:15:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap: procurement path, PO vs card, and approvals mapping (Acme Corp)

Hi Sarah —

Thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on procurement and approvals: 

Recap from discovery:
- Use case: platform search + personalization (production inference at 500 req/s peak).
- Timeline: target pilot start mid-March, production by end of Q2.
- Compliance: SOC 2 required; legal will need standard DPA (we can provide).

Key qualification points we discussed we need to lock down:
1) Procurement path: PO vs card — you mentioned procurement manages large commitments via PO. Can you confirm whether payments will come via a PO (cental procurement) or corporate card for pilot?
2) Marketplace interest: Is Acme open to procuring via AWS Marketplace / GCP Marketplace (faster billing + 3rd-party marketplace incentives)?
3) Budget & approvals: please confirm the economic buyer and finance sponsor (name/title), and who is the signatory for contracts > $100k.

Proposed next steps:
- If procurement uses PO: please share the procurement contact + PO template (we can fill and return).
- I’ll share a short SOW draft + pricing for pilot (attached).
- If you want marketplace fast-track, I can loop in our partnerships team — let me know.

I’ll follow up with a SOW and a PO template we usually fill for enterprise customers.

Thanks again — looking forward to moving fast on this.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
---
Attachments: redwood_sow_draft_v1.pdf (SOW draft, pricing ranges)

From: Sarah Jones <sarah.jones@acme-corp.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2026 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: procurement path, PO vs card, and approvals mapping (Acme Corp)

Thanks Aditya — great recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Procurement path: We do prefer PO for anything with term commitments. For the pilot (30–60 days, <$10k) we can use a corporate card, but production commitments will require a PO and a contract. Procurement (procurement@acme-corp.com) will own the PO process.

2) Marketplace: We prefer direct vendor invoicing for larger contracts, but if Redwood has an AWS Marketplace offering with consolidated billing and an enterprise listing, that could be attractive for procurement. We'll evaluate both.

3) Budget & approvals:
- Economic buyer: Daniel Park, CTO (daniel.park@acme-corp.com) — owns budget for platform initiatives.
- Finance sponsor: Marcus Liu, Finance Manager (procurement@acme-corp.com) will help with PO creation and budgeting cadence.
- Signatory: VP of Legal (exec signatory for contracts > $100k) — we'll need legal review on the SOW + DPA.

Can you send an updated SOW and a filled PO template to procurement@acme-corp.com? Also please include expected MRR/annualized cost ranges so I can surface to Daniel.

If you want, we can set up a short session with procurement this week to walk them through the PO steps.

Sarah
Director, Product Partnerships
Acme Corp

To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2026 11:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: procurement path, PO vs card, and approvals mapping (Acme Corp)

Looping in internal next actions based on Sarah's reply — internal only.

Notes:
- Economic buyer = Daniel Park (CTO) — set up a 20-min CTO briefing to cover value/op-ex savings and production SLAs. Aditya to own.
- Finance sponsor / procurement contact = procurement@acme-corp.com (Marcus Liu) — they need a filled PO template.
- Signatory = VP Legal — legal review required; send DPA + SOW to legal for redlines.

Recommended sprint:
1) Aditya: update SOW with MRR/annualized ranges and a 30-day pilot pricing (no long-term commitment). Attach the filled PO template.
2) Marissa: prep a short one-pager on SLAs and uptime to send to procurement/CTO.
3) Vivek: check marketplace options and note implications for discounts and billing terms (if they prefer AWS Marketplace vs direct invoicing).

I'll queue a HubSpot task and mark deal "needs procurement meeting". If we want to push marketplace, we should mention the faster procurement timeline as a benefit.

-Lauren
VP, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Jones <sarah.jones@acme-corp.com>, procurement@acme-corp.com
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 09:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: procurement path, PO vs card, and approvals mapping (Acme Corp)

Hi Sarah / Procurement team —

Thanks for the details. Per our internal notes (cc'd Lauren/Marissa), attached are: 
- redwood_sow_draft_v1.pdf (updated to include pilot pricing, MRR/annualized ranges)
- acme_po_template.pdf (we filled the common fields where possible)

Pilot pricing summary (high level):
- 30-day pilot (up to 100k inference tokens/day): $4,500 one-time set-up + $0.06 per 1k tokens over usage threshold — estimated monthly $6k–$9k depending on ramp.
- Production estimate (example scale): $4k–$12k/month depending on sustained throughput and quantization profile (we'll refine after pilot metrics).

Ask from procurement:
1) If you confirm PO is the right path for production, please send an initial PO to procurement@acme-corp.com referencing deal ACME-2026-0421 and we will route to finance for invoice terms.
2) If you prefer Marketplace, tell us which provider (AWS/GCP) and we will prioritize a marketplace quote (may impact discounting).
3) Please confirm signatory timeline — if legal requires standard redlines we'll target a 7–10 business day review.

Next steps I propose:
- I’ll schedule a 20-min meeting with Daniel (CTO) to walk the value + SLA tradeoffs (propose Wed next week). Please let me know availability.
- Procurement: If you can confirm PO contact and send the initial PO, we’ll turn around countersigned SOW + DPA within 3 business days (assuming standard comments).

Thanks — happy to jump on a call with procurement and Daniel to accelerate.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
